stem.en: A balsam plant is not watered for some days, and its leaves droop. What has changed inside its leaf cells?

text.en: Their vacuoles have lost water, so the cells are less firm.

feedback.en: Yes. Less water in the vacuole means less pressure inside the cell.

text.en: Their cell walls have melted away, so nothing holds the leaf up.

feedback.en: The wall stays in place. Water and pressure are what changed.

text.en: Their chloroplasts have moved into the vacuole, away from the sun.

feedback.en: Chloroplasts stay in the cytoplasm. They do not hold a leaf up.

text.en: The cells have divided into smaller cells that take up less room.

feedback.en: Drooping does not need any division. It happens to the cells already there.

explanation.en: When a plant does not get enough water, the vacuole loses water, the cells become less firm, and the plant wilts.

hints.en: Which organelle stores most of the water in a plant cell?
